parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is in the application layer. Its main job, coordinating order creation and lookup through a repository, fits that layer. The problem is that it also takes on transport (presentation-layer) concerns. `findOne(id: string, request?: Request)` accepts an Express HTTP `Request` object. The method never uses it, but it ties the use-case signature to the HTTP framework. The service also throws HTTP-specific exceptions (`BadRequestException` and `NotFoundException` from @nestjs/common, which map to 400 and 404 responses). That puts the choice of HTTP status codes in the application layer, when it belongs in presentation, for example a controller or exception filter. Throwing NestJS HTTP exceptions from a service is a common idiom, so that point alone would be weak. The Express `Request` parameter is the clearer sign that transport has leaked into the layer. A lesser point: the domain invariant (quantity must be positive) and the total calculation sit in the service rather than in the domain entity. I did not count this as a violation, because application services often do this kind of orchestration.

violations.message: OrderService.findOne takes an Express `Request` parameter (`request?: Request`). That is an HTTP transport concern, and it belongs in the presentation layer (controller), not the application layer.

OrderService.create and findOne throw the HTTP-specific BadRequestException and NotFoundException, so the application layer is choosing HTTP status codes. Mapping errors to HTTP responses belongs in the presentation layer (controller or exception filter). The service should throw application or domain errors instead.
